key_insight: Machine-learned dynamics reveals that small polarons at reduced TiO2(110) surfaces move far more slowly than in bulk because surface hopping pathways are strongly constrained.
engineering_relevance: This helps explain low electron mobility in porous rutile TiO2 and guides surface/defect engineering for better charge transport in oxides used for catalysis, photovoltaics, batteries, and energy storage.
method: Extended machine-learning-assisted polaron dynamics to a reducible oxide surface
Simulated oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110) for several nanoseconds across temperatures
Analyzed polaron hopping pathways and vacancy-induced free-energy bias
evidence_signal: Long-timescale simulations show surface polaron mobility is suppressed by several orders of magnitude relative to bulk, with motion mainly confined to planar inter-row hops and only rare interlayer events.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated on oxygen-deficient rutile TiO2(110), so transferability to other surfaces and defect chemistries still needs validation.
paper_title: Machine-learned dynamics of surface polarons at reduced oxide surfaces
